turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Honestly, a little stressed, but okay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you do a quick mock interview with me? Just one question.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure. Tell me about a time you made a mistake at work, and what you did about it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Just so I know, Grace, are you home for dinner tomorrow?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I ask about something else? I've got a five hour train ride tomorrow and I want to bring something to play.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hold your thoughts until I've described all the options.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My handheld has a long role playing game I started months ago and never finished.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's also a puzzle app on my phone with hundreds of short levels, no internet needed.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I could take my old retro handheld with a few classic platformers, tiny and the battery lasts forever.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or I bring a book of logic puzzles and a pen and give screens a rest.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'm done describing. Be my tiebreaker.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: I'd bring the handheld with the long game and finally get into it, then switch to the phone puzzles. The retro console is fun but you might finish those games fast, and the book is nice if you want a break from screens.
